Constraint-based CPDAG discovery

Source: R/cpdag.R
mc_graph_pipeline.Rd

Two-phase structure learning, self-contained in mcglmgraph, that estimates the completed partially directed acyclic graph (CPDAG) of the Markov equivalence class of the directed acyclic graph (DAG) underlying the second-order dependence between the responses. Phase one recovers the skeleton and the separating sets from the between-response covariance via mc_pc_skeleton. Phase two orients the edges up to the Markov equivalence class: the native route (orient_method = "pc") orients v-structures by the separating-set rule and then applies Meek's rules; the optional route ("hc" or "tabu") delegates the second phase to bnlearn's score-based search. A blacklist prevents arcs outside the native skeleton, but the score search may remove native skeleton edges; this route is therefore not a pure orientation of a fixed skeleton.

Usage

mc_graph_pipeline(
  fit,
  alpha = 0.05,
  orient_method = c("pc", "hc", "tabu"),
  orient_rule = c("standard", "conservative", "majority"),
  required = NULL,
  forbidden = NULL,
  max_ord = NULL,
  df_residual = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_cpdag'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

alpha

significance level of the second-order separation test.

orient_method

"pc" (native, default), "hc" or "tabu" (bnlearn). When bnlearn is not installed, the last two fall back on "pc" with a warning, and the result records it in orientation_fallback.

orient_rule

rule for the unshielded triples of the native route: "standard" (default), "conservative" or "majority". It has no effect when orient_method is a score-based route.

required, forbidden

optional background knowledge, as two-column matrices of arcs \((from, to)\) given either by response name or by index. An arc in required must be present with that direction, an arc in forbidden must not. They are imposed before propagation, and Meek's fourth rule, idle without them, carries their consequences through the rest of the graph. Available on the native route only.

max_ord

maximum conditioning order; NULL uses \(R - 2\).

df_residual

optional residual degrees of freedom \(\nu_e\): NULL (default) uses the raw-sample contract based on \(n\); a number or the result of mc_residual_df is used as given; "auto" computes it with mc_residual_df and refuses a fit for which it is not exact.

x

an object of class "mcg_cpdag".

...

ignored.

Value

An object of class "mcg_cpdag", a list with the 0/1 matrix skeleton of the oriented structure and its edges (two-column integer matrix); the constraint-stage pc_skeleton and sepset, as returned by mc_pc_skeleton; the cpdag adjacency in the convention of mc_orient_meek, labeled by response; the vstructures table (NULL on a score-based route); the conflicts table of edges required in opposite directions; the named logical vector gates; the logical valid_cpdag; the label to be used when reporting the output; knowledge and n_imposed, the background knowledge with the checks on it and the number of arcs it oriented; orient_method, orient_rule, orient_method_requested and orientation_fallback; sepsets, the collections enumerated under a rule other than "standard" (NULL otherwise); ambiguous, the triples left undecided, and their number n_ambiguous; meek_iterations and meek_blocked, the number of sweeps of Meek's rules and of orientations withheld by an ambiguous triple; separation_diagnostics, the diagnostics of the skeleton search; and alpha, df_residual and response_names. The print method returns x invisibly.

Which separating sets the orientation consults

orient_rule selects between the rule that reads the single set the skeleton recorded ("standard") and the two rules that enumerate every set separating the endpoints of each unshielded triple on the final skeleton, "conservative" and "majority". The enumeration is native and uses the same conditional-association test and the same degrees-of-freedom contract as the skeleton, so a difference between two runs is attributable to the rule and not to a change of test. A triple that the rule leaves ambiguous receives no orientation, and Meek's R1, R3 and R4 are withheld where they would settle it by propagation; the count is reported in n_ambiguous.

What background knowledge changes

Without it the output is the CPDAG of an equivalence class, the object the second-order separations identify. With it the output is no longer the CPDAG of any class: when no triple is left ambiguous it is the maximally oriented partially directed graph of Meek (1995), the union of the members of the class that satisfy the knowledge. The label records which of the two it is, and knowledge carries the arcs that were imposed. Knowledge is refused, rather than silently dropped, when it contradicts itself, when it requires an arc between responses the skeleton does not join, and when it contradicts an edge oriented by a v-structure. A contradiction with an edge that only Meek's rules would orient is not refused beforehand: it surfaces during propagation as a conflict or a cycle and the output then fails the checks below.

What the output may be called

The output is submitted to seven checks, reported in gates: no pair of colliders or of rules required opposite directions on an edge (no_orientation_conflict); no separation test needed a ridge to invert its block (unregularized_separation); the orientation stayed within the learned skeleton (orientation_within_skeleton) and kept all of it (skeleton_preserved); the directed part has no cycle (acyclic); every collider that was written survives Meek propagation (vstructures_preserved); and a consistent DAG extension exists, by the algorithm of Dor and Tarsi (1992) (consistent_extension). When all pass, valid_cpdag is TRUE and label is "CPDAG", or "maximally oriented graph under background knowledge" when the knowledge oriented some edge. When any fails, valid_cpdag is FALSE and label becomes "second-order partially directed structure": the object still records what the separations supported, but it is not certified as the CPDAG of a Markov equivalence class. The first two checks record facts of the run and not properties of the returned graph, so a refused label does not establish that the output differs from the CPDAG of a class. A triple left ambiguous by the conservative or majority rule stays unoriented, so a certified output can be less oriented than the CPDAG of the class of its extension.

Assumptions behind the reading

Passing the checks is a statement about internal consistency only. Reading the output as the CPDAG of the second-order structure assumes that the between-response covariance is generated by some DAG and that every zero partial correlation corresponds to a d-separation in it (second-order Markov and faithfulness). Reading it as the Markov equivalence class of the distribution of the responses assumes, in addition, that a zero partial correlation of the residuals is equivalent to conditional independence of the responses given the conditioning responses and the covariates, which holds for jointly Gaussian residuals whose conditional covariance does not depend on the covariates and fails in general otherwise. Recovery of the class is asymptotic, for a fixed number of responses and a level alpha that decreases with the sample size. A causal reading of the arcs requires further causal sufficiency, absence of selection bias and substantive justification. The procedure checks none of these assumptions.

References

Spirtes, P., Glymour, C. and Scheines, R. (2000). Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd edition. MIT Press.

Meek, C. (1995). Causal inference and causal explanation with background knowledge. Proceedings of the 11th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 403-410.

Dor, D. and Tarsi, M. (1992). A simple algorithm to construct a consistent extension of a partially oriented graph. Technical Report R-185, Cognitive Systems Laboratory, University of California, Los Angeles.

Andersson, S. A., Madigan, D. and Perlman, M. D. (1997). A characterization of Markov equivalence classes for acyclic digraphs. The Annals of Statistics 25(2), 505-541. doi:10.1214/aos/1031833662

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 600
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n); z3 <- 0.7*z1 + 0.7*z2 + rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = z1, y2 = z2, y3 = z3, x = rnorm(n))
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x, y2~x, y3~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_graph_pipeline(f)$cpdag
#>    y1 y2 y3
#> y1  0  0  1
#> y2  0  0  1
#> y3  0  0  0
# }
